correctness.rationale: Exact block-matrix spectral reduction is proved for every integer N>=2 and 1<=k<N; the common extinction benchmark strictly exceeds each possible diagonal quotient term, so determinant signs give an iff test. The continuous ratio has one derivative sign transition, permitting only floor/ceiling integer minima. Algebraic square completion gives the exact rounding identity and equality cases. The N=5 example is established by rational inequalities; packaged checker independently diagonalizes 21,309 full-matrix instances and checks 1,200 brute finite optima.

Choe and Lee 2015 (doi:10.1186/s12976-015-0026-x) computes two-group reproduction numbers and analyzes preferred mixing/treatment strategies, not fixed-census minimum cross-link weight.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broad spectral persistence theorem reduces the scientific object to a positive matrix, but it does not itself optimize the required link rate over allowed integer group sizes. General partition eigenvalue theorems likewise cover Step 1 but leave the integer optimization and exact rounding-defect identity unassessed. All such basic results are credited as coverage, not counted as original.

originality.rationale: The key exact finite-design contribution is an all-compositions integer cross-link threshold, a two-candidate rule, and an exact strictly positive rounding excess for noninteger relaxed optima. Full-text comparison was available for the closest 2015 landscape and heterogeneous-mixing articles. Earlier foundational spectral and equitable-partition results explicitly cover ingredients but no inspected evidence establishes this integer optimization. The inaccessible historical full texts and supplement remain nontrivial risks; priority is not independently certified.
residual_risks: An older specialized block-metapopulation analysis may contain the same discrete threshold even if current searches found none.
The foundational 2001 and adjacent 2009 studies were not fully read, and the supplemental PLOS PDF was inaccessible.
Equitable partition and Perron threshold mathematics are established; broad spectral optimization literature may derive an equivalent integer minimization without habitat terminology.
The new contribution is intentionally finite and model-specific, and independent historical-priority review has not occurred.

value.rationale: When both homogeneous networks fail a spectral persistence-capacity benchmark, the exact minimum cross-habitat coupling over feasible integer patch counts is a motivated conservation-network design invariant. Its explicit floor/ceiling rule replaces an unbounded-in-N count search with two checks, and its exact discrepancy quantifies when continuous habitat-fraction planning predicts supercriticality absent from any realizable finite census. The N=5 case exhibits a strict interval of such disagreement, without claiming stochastic survival or general spatial embedding.
